name: price-transparency
title: Price transparency
description: Show where the money goes: a stacked bar of materials, making, shipping, duties and margin, with the typical retail price beside it.
docs: price is what the customer pays, in minor units; parts are { label, amount, note? } in minor units, in the order they are drawn. The bar is computed from the parts: a part with no money in it is left out, when the parts add up to less than the price the rest is drawn dashed as 'Other costs', and when they add up to more the price is what they add up to, so the bar always sums to the price; with no usable part at all the bar and the list are left out and the price stands alone, never as zero, and the comparison with the retail price still works. Every part is also a row with its amount and its share, the shares are whole percentages that add up to exactly 100, and the bar is hidden from screen readers because the list carries every number. A part's note opens from its name in a popover named after the part; hovering or focusing a row lights its part of the bar. retail is the typical retail price: with it the panel says how much lower this price is and shows both figures, without it there is nothing to compare. note is the small print under everything (what the figures are based on and when they were checked). currency and locale write the amounts and percentages, title and description name the product, headingAs is 'h3' inside a section that has its own h2, and labels holds the fixed words.
